A small physical state can predict a controlled record without closing the exact measurement hierarchy

I have completed a restricted quantum construction that sharpens the state-selection principle:

Retain the variables needed to follow the known driving and persistent hidden modes. Additional correlations created by measurement can be omitted when their influence on every permitted route to future observations is quantitatively bounded.

The construction gives a positive, closed law for the entire permitted classical record under feedback. It has two explicit realizations:

Interacting spins: seven real variables for two persistent classical modes, independent of the number of spins, for a specified aggregate measurement and reset architecture.
Fermionic matter: one covariance matrix per persistent mode, with a spatial window bound that does not require hopping to be weaker than damping.

These are scoped mathematical results. They do not establish a general effective theory of interacting matter, identify an unknown material’s kinetic structure, or demonstrate a computational advantage. Their significance is that they provide a justified way to avoid an otherwise growing conditional correlation hierarchy while preserving a complete experimental record to a stated accuracy.
